---
title: Slots: a parameter that is itself a composable
version: 1
---

**A slot is a parameter of type `@Composable () -> Unit`**, and it lets the caller decide part of
what a component shows. `Button` does not know whether its label is text, an icon, or both; it
takes a slot and draws whatever the caller puts in it inside its own frame, padding and click
handling. Almost every Material component is built this way, and `Scaffold`, which lays out a whole
screen, has five: `topBar`, `bottomBar`, `snackbarHost`, `floatingActionButton` and `content`.

The planner gets a card with a title, used for every block of the home screen:

```kotlin
// app/src/main/java/com/example/planner/ui/PlannerCard.kt
package com.example.planner.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.material3.Card
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.example.planner.data.sampleCourses

@Composable
fun PlannerCard(title: String, content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    Card {
        Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp)) {
            Text(title, style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge)
            content()
        }
    }
}

@Preview(showBackground = true)
@Composable
fun PlannerCardPreview() {
    MaterialTheme {
        PlannerCard(title = "This week") {
            CourseRow(sampleCourses[0], minutesThisWeek = 95)
            CourseRow(sampleCourses[2], minutesThisWeek = 50)
        }
    }
}
```

`content()` is a call: the card emits its title and then runs the caller's lambda, so the two rows
are emitted inside the card's column, after the title. **The card owns the frame and the caller owns
what goes in it.** `PlannerCard` will hold the week's summary, a course's sessions and a list of
reminders, and it never has to learn about any of them. The `"This week"` in the preview is sample
data, which is why it is not in `strings.xml`.

## When a slot is the wrong tool

A slot is right when the caller should decide **what** goes in a region. It is wrong when the caller
only needs to pass **data** the component already knows how to show. A `CourseRow` taking a slot for
the course name would let every caller draw the name differently, which is a design system with no
design. Prefer a plain parameter until two real callers need different content in the same place,
and then make it a slot.
